summary: Friedberg projects Starlink could grow from 4 million to 100 million or more subscribers, potentially becoming one of the largest subscription businesses on earth, driven by satellite-to-phone expansion.
quote: Starlink's running at 4 million subs right now. That's like $100 a month, 4 million subs... If we can get satellite to phone and you can get Starlink more broadly available, this could be a 100 million subscriber business.

summary: Chamath argues Expedia is a fragile UI layer on top of licensed third-party data that AI agents will disintermediate, making a $30B acquisition price far too expensive for the risk.

summary: Friedberg sees a financial case for Uber acquiring Expedia at ~4x pro forma EBITDA given Dara's operational knowledge and cross-sell potential, but acknowledges significant strategic risk from AI disintermediation.
quote: if you can bump the EBITDA up to $6 billion a year, that's a pretty low multiple. I mean, you could kind of see yourself rationalizing this just from a financial basis that you're paying 4 times EBITDA to buy this thing.

summary: Sacks is skeptical of the Uber/Expedia cross-sell thesis, arguing Uber users have no intent to book hotels via the Uber app, making the synergy rationale an MBA-style handwave that won't hold up in practice.
quote: I don't think Uber customers want to be cross-sold on booking a hotel... I'm never going to think to go on my Uber app for that... The only time I open the Uber app is when I want to hail a taxi.

summary: Chamath argues Uber would be making a poor capital allocation decision by acquiring Expedia for $30B, when AI agents will soon render travel UI businesses worthless; he suggests buying Waymo would be a far better use of capital.

summary: Friedberg reiterates his prediction to buy uranium stocks, arguing nuclear energy is a necessity to meet growing global energy demand — even pre-AI buildout — and that there is simply no way to meet energy demand without nuclear. He frames uranium as a structural long.
quote: I did, I think, talk about this a year ago. It was also my prediction for the year was to by the uranium stocks predicated on what I think is a really important point... there is no way to meet the energy demand without nuclear.
